text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When your code doesn't work as expected, the first step is to identify the bug. This means carefully reading error messages and examining which part of the code might be causing the problem. Instead of guessing, you should follow a systematic approach: reproduce the issue, form a hypothesis, test it, and then fix the error. There are many debugging tools available, such as setting breakpoints in an IDE to pause the program and inspect variables. Additionally, logging is a simple yet powerful technique. By adding print statements or log messages to your code, you can track the flow of execution and see exactly what values are being used, which makes finding the root cause much easier.
